description: This format is common for applied mathematics, numerical analysis, and mathematical modeling papers. It focuses on theory, methods, numerical validation, and analysis of results.

sections.Introduction: A brief overview of the research problem, objectives, and motivation.

sections.Theoretical Basis: Background on the mathematical theory, methods, or models that are used in the paper.

sections.Methodology: Explanation of the approach or methods developed or applied in the research.

sections.Numerical Results: Presentation of numerical experiments, data, and results obtained using the proposed methods.

sections.Analysis: Interpretation of the numerical results, comparison with theory or other methods.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of any support or funding received during the research.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of the findings and potential directions for future research.

description: This format is typical for physics papers, especially in theoretical and experimental physics, focusing on explaining new findings or experimental setups.

sections.Introduction: Overview of the problem and objectives, with a brief summary of relevant background.

sections.Theory and Models: Presentation of the theoretical framework or models used to analyze the problem.

sections.Methodology/Experimental Setup: Details about the experimental methods, setup, or simulations performed.

sections.Results: Presentation of experimental or theoretical results, often including graphs and tables.

sections.Discussion: Interpretation of results in the context of the theory and comparison with previous work.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of contributions, funding, or support.

sections.Conclusions: Concluding remarks and potential implications or future work.

description: This format is common in social sciences (e.g., sociology, psychology, economics) with a focus on theory, research questions, and empirical validation.

sections.Introduction: Introduction to the research problem, its importance, and objectives.

sections.Literature Review: Review of existing literature and theoretical frameworks relevant to the research.

sections.Research Questions/Hypotheses: Clear presentation of the research questions or hypotheses being tested.

sections.Methodology: Explanation of the research design, sampling, and data collection methods.

sections.Results: Presentation of statistical analyses or qualitative findings.

sections.Discussion: Interpretation of results in relation to the hypotheses and existing literature.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of any assistance or funding.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of findings and suggestions for future research or practical applications.

description: This structure is common in agricultural sciences, agronomic sciences, biology and health sciences, where experiments or observations are the focus and methods need to be reproducible.

sections.Introduction: Introduction to the research question, background, and objectives.

sections.Background: Review of relevant biological concepts, previous research, or disease models.

sections.Materials and Methods: Detailed description of the materials, techniques, and experimental methods used.

sections.Results: Presentation of experimental data, often with figures and tables.

sections.Discussion: Interpretation of the results, comparison with previous research, and possible clinical implications.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of any financial or academic support.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of results, implications for practice, and future research directions.

description: In chemistry and chemical engineering, this format is used to report on experimental methods, systems design, and reactions or materials.

sections.Introduction: Introduction to the chemical problem, its significance, and the objectives of the study.

sections.Literature Review: Overview of previous research and relevant chemical theories or models.

sections.Experimental Section/Materials and Metho: Detailed description of the chemical experiments, procedures, and equipment used.

sections.Results and Discussion: Presentation and analysis of experimental data, with a focus on interpreting results.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of contributions, resources, or funding.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of findings, implications for chemical processes, and possible future research.

description: This format is used for computer science and software engineering papers, where systems or algorithms are developed and tested.

sections.Introduction (with related works):
Introduction to the problem in the context of the state of the art, the goals of the research, and the motivation. Use the format:
1. General context of the topic.
 2. Specific problem within the topic that the text focuses on.
3. Specific computational problem addressed.
4. Proposed computational solution.
5. Obtained results.

sections.System Design/Methodology: Detailed description of the algorithms, models, or systems being proposed or implemented.

sections.Implementation: Explanation of the implementation of the proposed system or algorithm.

sections.Experiments and Results: Presentation of benchmarks, performance data, and experimental results.

sections.Discussion: Analysis of results, comparison with other approaches, and limitations.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of any support or resources.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of the contributions, results, and potential future work.

description: This format is typical for philosophy and humanities papers, where the focus is on logical argumentation, analysis, and critique of existing ideas.

sections.Introduction: Introduction to the central research question, context, and goals of the paper.

sections.Literature Review: Review of existing philosophical literature and key concepts.

sections.Thesis or Research Question: Presentation of the central thesis or research question the paper seeks to address.

sections.Argumentation: Logical development of arguments, philosophical analysis, or critique.

sections.Discussion: Reflection on the implications of the arguments and potential counterarguments.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of any support or contributions.

sections.Conclusions: Concluding summary of the arguments and future directions for research.

description: In economics and political science, this format is used to present theoretical models or empirical data related to policy or economic issues.

sections.Introduction: Overview of the research problem, its importance, and objectives.

sections.Literature Review: Review of relevant theories, models, and previous research in the field.

sections.Research Design/Methodology: Explanation of the research methods, data collection, and analysis techniques.

sections.Results: Presentation of empirical results, often with statistical analyses or case studies.

sections.Discussion: Interpretation of the results in relation to theories and real-world implications.

sections.Acknowledgment: Acknowledgment of support, data sources, or collaborations.

sections.Conclusions: Summary of findings, policy implications, and suggestions for future research.
